source.title: Social Studies Grade 8 (KICD Junior School Curriculum Design, first published 2023, Revised 2024)
source.publisher: Kenya Institute of Curriculum Development (KICD) — mirrored via teacherspalace.co.ke
source.notes: WebFetch reported it could not parse the raw PDF stream but saved the file locally; the Read tool then parsed the full 69-page PDF text natively and verbatim (not summarized by an intermediate model). Cover page reads 'KENYA INSTITUTE OF CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT / JUNIOR SCHOOL CURRICULUM DESIGN / SOCIAL STUDIES / GRADE 8', ISBN 978-9914-43-789-8, First published 2023, Revised 2024 — this matches the confirmed official filename 'Social Studies Grade 8 - Revised.pdf' independently verified from KICD's own Google Drive index (file ID 1yx30v28nVLKYSByRB9G2Omalh76-ZL6h) on the Grade 8 designs page, and the mirror's own filename ('social-studies-grade-8-revised-1...'). All 5 strands and 15 sub-strands below were read verbatim from the 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB-STRANDS' table (p.xii) and cross-checked against each strand's detailed section (pp.13-58). Four sub-strands carry a bulleted list of named topics directly under the sub-strand heading in the detailed section (Early Civilisation: Asia/Europe; Weather and Climate: Desert/Semi-desert/Tropical/Mediterranean/Mountain; Peaceful Conflict Resolution: Negotiation/Mediation/Arbitration; Historical Sites and Monuments in Africa: Fort Jesus/Kilwa/Great Zimbabwe/Giza pyramids/Meroe/Timbuktu/Robben Island) — these are recorded as subSubStrands, following the same convention used for Grade 9 Mathematics in this repo. Two sub-strand names differ minutely between the summary table and the detailed section: the summary table says 'Early Civilisations' and 'Peaceful Conflict Resolutions' (plural), while the detailed section headings read 'Early Civilisation' and 'Peaceful Conflict Resolution' (singular) — the singular detailed-section wording is used here as canonical, per the precedent set in this repo's Grade 8 Pre-Technical Studies file. This design differs structurally from Grade 9 Social Studies in that it explicitly bundles 'Community Service Learning' as its own numbered strand (2.0) with a single sub-strand, rather than treating CSL purely as an appendix; Grade 8 also includes a distinct Appendix I with a 6-milestone CSL implementation guide not present in this JSON (out of scope — this file captures only the graded strands/sub-strands, not the appendices).

subStrands.name: Self-Improvement
specificLearningOutcomes: describe personality traits for self-understanding
share goals for self-improvement in social life
appreciate the role of values in the development of personality traits
keyInquiryQuestions: Which animal best reflects your personal characteristics?
What career choices in Social Studies relate to you?

subStrands.name: Self-Esteem Assessment
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the contribution of self-esteem on their holistic development
determine effects of unhealthy self-esteem in day-to-day social lives
assess their self-esteem in social interactions
desire to improve their self-esteem for personal productivity
keyInquiryQuestions: How does self-esteem affect my holistic development?

subStrands.name: Community Service Learning Project
specificLearningOutcomes: identify a problem/gap in the community
design solution(s) to the identified problem
plan to implement the solution to the identified problem
implement plan for solving the identified problem
report/account on the concluded project
appreciate the need to offer solutions to the gaps/challenges in the community
keyInquiryQuestions: How does one determine some gaps/ needs in the community?
Why is it necessary to make adequate preparations before embarking on a project?

subStrands.name: Scientific Theory about Human Origin
specificLearningOutcomes: explore scientific theory about human origin
illustrate changes that took place in humans as a result of evolution
draw conclusions on origin of humanity based on the scientific theory
illustrate strategies of preservation of remains of early humans
develop reasons why Africa is considered as the cradle for humanity
recognise reasons why Africa as the cradle of humanity
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is Africa considered as the cradle of humanity?

subStrands.name: Early Civilisation
specificLearningOutcomes: describe Swahili civilisation along the East African coast
show how best practices from early civilisations have contributed to the modern world
appreciate best practices of early civilisation to the development of the modern world
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is cultural heritage important to society?
subStrands.notes: Summary of Strands table (p.xii) names this sub-strand 'Early Civilisations' (plural); the detailed section heading (p.24) reads 'Early Civilisation' (singular) — the singular detailed-section wording is used here as canonical.

subStrands.name: Trans Saharan Slave Trade
specificLearningOutcomes: identify factors that led to development of Trans-Saharan slave Trade in Africa
describe organisation of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa
outline effects of Trans-Saharan slave trade in Africa
demonstrate assertiveness in promotion of social justice
desire to promote social justice in a society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do people subject others to slave trade?

subStrands.name: Population Growth in Africa
specificLearningOutcomes: explore causes and effects of population growth in Africa
examine types and effects of migration in Africa
illustrate demographic trends in Kenya
create awareness on the effects of population growth in the community
appreciate the impact of migration on population growth in Africa
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to study demographic changes?

subStrands.name: Diversity and interpersonal skills
specificLearningOutcomes: explore social cultural diversities in Kenya
explain ways of building a healthy self-esteem in diverse social cultural society
describe the impact of emotions on self and others
manage peer pressure in a culturally diverse environment
appreciate social cultural diversities in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we demonstrate respect and appreciation of social cultural diversity and inclusion?

subStrands.name: Peaceful Conflict Resolution
specificLearningOutcomes: identify situations that lead to conflicts in the family
apply peaceful ways of resolving conflicts in the family
design strategies for effective communication in resolving conflicts
build healthy relationships to promote peace in the family
show empathy with survivors of conflicts in the family
appreciate the culture of peace in a society
keyInquiryQuestions: How can resolving conflicts help us live peacefully in the community?
subStrands.notes: Summary of Strands table (p.xii) names this sub-strand 'Peaceful Conflict Resolutions' (plural); the detailed section heading (p.32) reads 'Peaceful Conflict Resolution' (singular) — the singular detailed-section wording is used here as canonical.

subStrands.name: Map Reading and Interpretation
specificLearningOutcomes: interpret maps using marginal information
calculate areas of places on a topographical map
describe the different methods of representing physical features on topographical maps
apply critical thinking skills in map interpretation
value map reading and interpretation in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: How can critical thinking be used in map interpretation?

subStrands.name: Weather and Climate
specificLearningOutcomes: examine factors influencing climate in Africa
illustrate distribution and characteristics of major climatic regions of Africa
explore positive ways of managing disaster-related stress
apply problem-solving skills in addressing effects of climate change on the environment
recognise the effects of climate on human activities
keyInquiryQuestions: How does climate change affect human activities?
How can one manage stress during disasters?

subStrands.name: Vegetation in Africa
specificLearningOutcomes: explain factors influencing vegetation distribution in Africa
describe the characteristics of major vegetation regions of Africa on the map
locate the major vegetation regions of Africa
apply methods of conserving vegetation in the community
explore personal interests in conservation of vegetation for career exploration
appreciate vegetation conservation for environmental sustainability
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we care for vegetation in our environment?

subStrands.name: Historical Sites and Monuments in Africa
specificLearningOutcomes: locate selected historical sites and monuments in Africa
examine the importance of historical sites and monuments for the preservation of cultural heritage
explore ways of conserving historical sites and monuments in Africa
apply ways of conserving cultural heritage in community
desire to conserve historical sites and monuments in the locality in promoting cultural heritage
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we conserve historical sites and monuments?

subStrands.name: The Constitution of Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: explore components of the Constitution of Kenya
illustrate roles of the three arms of government of Kenya in reference to the relevant chapters in the Constitution
examine guiding principles of leadership and integrity in the Constitution of Kenya
apply assertiveness in upholding principles of leadership and integrity in daily interactions
exhibit good leadership intended in chapter six of the Constitution of Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we need a constitution?
Why is assertiveness important in adhering to the Constitution of Kenya?

subStrands.name: Human Rights
specificLearningOutcomes: explore how human rights can be respected and protected in the community
describe the process of effective communication on human rights issues
outline Children's Rights in Kenya
demonstrate ways in which children are protected against violation of their Rights in Kenya
recognise responsibility of the society in protecting human rights
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we promote respect for Children' Rights in the community?
How can effective communication foster respect for Human Rights?

subStrands.name: Citizenship
specificLearningOutcomes: describe qualities of a global citizen in an interconnected society
explore ways in which Nobel Prize nominees responded to injustice situations in the society
explain factors for harmonious coexistence among citizens in East Africa and Africa
exhibit social entrepreneurship and active participation in the community for personal and social well-being
show empathy to personalities who volunteer to address injustices in society
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we promote global citizenship?
How can we show empathy as global citizens?
subStrands.notes: Numbered '5.3' in the design but appears under a strand heading mislabelled '4.0 Political Developments and Governance' on p.53 of the source PDF (the correct strand number, per the Table of Contents and Summary of Strands table, is 5.0) — a typographical error in the source document itself, recorded here for transparency; this JSON uses the correct 5.0 strand grouping.
